This task uses a small rewriting calculus that is defined only here. You will write 5 terms in it.

CALCULUS
- A term is a symbol, or one term applied to another. Application is written by putting the two terms next to each other and it groups to the left: `F G H` means `(F G) H`. Parentheses group. Every symbol is a single letter, so spaces are optional.
- There are 5 constants, F, H, N, V, Z. Each has one rewrite rule (x, y, z stand for any terms):
    F x y z  ->  y (x z)
    H x y  ->  y
    N x y z  ->  x z (y z)
    V x y z  ->  x (z y)
    Z x y z  ->  y x z
- A rule can be used on any subterm in which the constant is followed by at least as many argument terms as its rule shows. The constant and those arguments are replaced by the right-hand side as one unit; any further arguments stay after it. The letters in the names carry no meaning beyond these rules.
- The lowercase symbols a, b, c have no rule. A term is finished when no rule can be used anywhere in it. Rewriting always takes the leftmost-outermost usable position first.
- Example with these rules: `H N N` applied to a, b, c rewrites as
    H N N a b c
    -> N a b c
    -> a c (b c)

TASKS
For each task give a term T built only from the constants F, H, N, V, Z (no a, b, c) such that `T a b c` rewrites to exactly the stated finished term within 2000 rewrite steps. The number of constant occurrences in T must not exceed the limit shown. A term within the limit exists for every task.

T1. T a b c  ->  b (a (a c (a c)))        (at most 7 constants)
T2. T a b c  ->  a (b c c) (a a (b c c))        (at most 7 constants)
T3. T a b c  ->  a b (b b) (b b) c        (at most 7 constants)
T4. T a b c  ->  a b c (b (a b (b b)) c)        (at most 7 constants)
T5. T a b c  ->  a (a a) (a a) (a b) c        (at most 7 constants)

ANSWER
Return exactly one ```python block that contains only this literal assignment and nothing else:

TERMS = {
    "T1": "<term>",
    "T2": "<term>",
    "T3": "<term>",
    "T4": "<term>",
    "T5": "<term>",
}

The block is parsed as a literal; any code makes the whole answer invalid. Score: one point per correct term; a wrong term costs nothing beyond its own point. Your whole reply, reasoning included, is cut off at 65,536 tokens, and a reply that is cut off scores 0 for every task. So budget your search: aim to finish within about 40,000 tokens of reasoning, and always give the block with your best candidate for every task, including the ones you could not settle.
